title: Bar Owner Steals the Show in Subway Improv With Conan O'Brien
summary:
It is not every day that running errands turns into an improv show with a famous comedian on the New York City subway. But that is exactly what happened to Debbie Shields, a Brooklyn bar owner who runs a comedy night.

Shields was on her way to see her accountant for her business when she struck up a conversation with comedian Conan O'Brien. She had no idea what she was walking into — and she was more than ready. 'If you give it to me, I give it right back to you,' she later said.

O'Brien was a guest on SubwayTakes, a popular internet talk show hosted by comedian Kareem Rahma, where everyday New Yorkers and celebrities humorously discuss their controversial opinions while riding the subway. Toward the end of O'Brien's episode, he apologized to Shields as she moved into an empty seat next to Rahma. The two shook hands and jumped into a spontaneous scene together, with O'Brien joking that they used to be married.

Shields fired back instantly: they had two kids. 'One's in medical school, the other one's in jail,' she said — and the former late-night host cracked up. Viewers said they loved her wit and her ability to keep up with O'Brien. He was impressed, too. O'Brien told New York Magazine he would love to work with Shields again. 'I'll do a sitcom with her,' he said. 'Or we can just hit the road, do a two-person show.'

Shields said she would love to collaborate again. Since the episode aired, she has become an internet sensation, with calls coming in from around the world — Japan at 1:30 in the morning, Australia, England. 'It's crazy right now,' she said. 'Oh boy, it's been busy.'

Not bad for a trip to the accountant.
why_it_matters: It shows how an unplanned moment can reach people around the world once it is shared online. It also shows that being ready to join in can open doors, since O'Brien now wants to work with Shields again.
